newsitem.title: INDIA: Seven Kashmiri guerrillas killed in encounters.
newsitem.headline: Seven Kashmiri guerrillas killed in encounters.

text.p: Indian paramilitary troops killed seven separatist guerrillas in two different encounters in the troubled Kashmir region, police said on Wednesday.
The police said in a statement that four people died in an encounter on Tuesday night between militants and a search party near Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
In an another incident, paramilitary troops on Wednesday shot dead three separatist guerrillas at Gungbug village, 20 km (12.5 miles) southwest of Srinagar, police said.
They said the militants were killed in a four-hour shootout after paramilitary troopers laid siege to a guerrilla hideout in the village.
More than a dozen groups, primarily Moslem militants, are fighting New Delhi's rule in the Himalayan state. Kashmir is the only Moslem-majority state in India, which is predominantly Hindu.
According to police and hospitals, more than 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year-old rebellion in the state.
